text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses labeled training data—examples that already have the correct answers. For instance, you might show it thousands of photos of dogs and cats, each tagged with its animal type. The computer then builds a model, which is essentially a set of rules or patterns it discovers from this data. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen photos, guessing whether each one shows a dog or a cat. To check how well it works, we measure its accuracy, which is the percentage of correct predictions on a separate test set.
